overview.title: No cluster connected yet

alerts.title: No alerts yet

hints.FailedGetResourceMetric: The metrics API (metrics.k8s.io) is not installed: install metrics-server, or remove the HPA.
hints.FailedComputeMetricsReplicas: The HPA can't read its metrics: install metrics-server, or check the HPA's metric names.
hints.FailedScheduling: No node fits the pod: check its requests, node selectors, taints and free capacity.
hints.FailedMount: A volume couldn't be mounted: check the Secret, ConfigMap or PVC it refers to.
hints.FailedAttachVolume: The volume couldn't attach: it may still be attached to another node.
hints.Unhealthy: A probe is failing: check the probe's path and port, and the app's startup time.
hints.BackOff: The container keeps exiting: open the pod for its last exit code and logs.
hints.ErrImagePull: The image couldn't be pulled: check the image name, tag and registry credentials.
hints.ImagePullBackOff: The image couldn't be pulled: check the image name, tag and registry credentials.
hints.FailedCreatePodSandBox: The pod's network couldn't be set up: check the CNI plugin on that node.
hints.Evicted: The node ran short of memory or disk and evicted the pod.
hints.OOMKilling: The kernel killed a process for memory: raise the memory limit or find the leak.
hints.FailedToCreateEndpoint: An Endpoints object with this name already exists: usually harmless after a Service is re-created.
hints.ClusterIPNotAllocated: Kubernetes repaired a Service's cluster IP: usually harmless.
hints.DNSConfigForming: The node's resolv.conf has too many search domains or nameservers.
hints.NodeNotReady: The node stopped reporting: check the kubelet and the node's network.

reasons.evicting: Keys are being evicted: {n} in the last 15 minutes. Writes push out old data.
reasons.no_maxmemory: No maxmemory is set: memory can grow until the container's limit, and then it is OOM-killed.
reasons.slow_keys_command: KEYS appears in the slow log ({n}×): it blocks the server while it walks every key. Use SCAN.
reasons.replica_down: A replica is disconnected from its primary.
reasons.save_failed: The last save to disk failed: a restart would lose data written since.
reasons.clients_rejected: {n} connections were refused in the last 15 minutes: maxclients is reached.
reasons.clients_blocked: {n} clients are blocked waiting (BLPOP, XREAD, WAIT…).
reasons.connections_near_max: Connections are at {pct}% of max_connections ({n} of {max}). Most are held by {top}.
reasons.long_query: A query has been running for {duration}.
reasons.idle_in_transaction: {n} sessions are idle in a transaction, the longest for {duration}: they hold locks and stop vacuum from cleaning up.
reasons.lock_waits: {n} sessions are waiting for a lock held by {who}.
reasons.deadlocks: {n} deadlocks in the last 15 minutes: the database cancelled one transaction each time.
reasons.slot_retains_wal: The inactive replication slot {slot} keeps {size} of WAL: the disk fills until it is used or dropped.
reasons.wraparound_risk: Transaction ID age in {db} is {n}: at 2,000 M PostgreSQL stops accepting writes. Vacuum is falling behind.
reasons.cache_hit_low: Only {pct}% of reads come from the cache: shared_buffers may be too small for the working set.
reasons.autovacuum_not_finishing: Autovacuum isn't finishing on {n} tables (for example {table}): dead rows rose for 24 hours with no autovacuum completed.
reasons.statements_unavailable: pg_stat_statements isn't installed: the query tables stay empty until it is.
reasons.errors_high: {pct}% of requests answer 5xx. Most come from {upstream} ({upstreamPct}%), last rolled out {rollout}.
reasons.upstream_no_endpoints: {upstream} has no ready endpoint: requests to it fail.
reasons.connections_dropped: {n} connections were dropped in the last 15 minutes: worker_connections is reached.
reasons.certificate_expiring: The certificate for {host} expires in {days} days.
reasons.ingress_metrics_off: ingress-nginx doesn't serve its metrics, so requests, errors and latency come from eBPF (plain HTTP only) and connections are missing. Turn them on (the controller pods restart):
reasons.stub_status_missing: Nginx has no stub_status, so connections are missing. Requests, errors and latency need nothing. Add this to its configuration and reload; WatchLog finds it on port 8080 or the service's port:
reasons.no_http_source: Requests, errors and latency come from the agents on the same host or cluster; this service, added by address, has none.
reasons.errors_high_upstream: {pct}% of requests answer 5xx. Most come from {upstream} ({upstreamPct}%).
reasons.stub_status_missing_tried: Nginx has no stub_status, so connections are missing. Requests, errors and latency need nothing. WatchLog looked at {tried}. Add this to its configuration and reload; WatchLog finds it on port 8080 or the service's port:
reasons.queue_no_consumers: {queue} has had no consumers since {since} and grows by {perMin} a minute ({ready} ready). {consumer}, connected to RabbitMQ until then, was {how} {when}.
reasons.queue_no_consumers_unknown: {queue} has had no consumers since {since} and grows by {perMin} a minute ({ready} ready). No client that was connected to RabbitMQ in the last 24 hours ended since.
reasons.queue_growing: {queue} grows by {perMin} a minute although it has consumers: they are slower than the publishers.
reasons.memory_alarm: {member} is in a memory alarm: publishers are blocked until memory drops below the high watermark.
reasons.disk_alarm: {member} is in a disk alarm: publishers are blocked until free disk is above the limit.
reasons.unacked_high: {n} messages are delivered but not acknowledged: consumers hold them without acking.
reasons.dead_letters_growing: {n} messages were dead-lettered in the last 15 minutes.
reasons.prometheus_plugin_off: The rabbitmq_prometheus plugin is off on {n} node(s), so WatchLog only sees whether RabbitMQ answers. Enable it (no restart needed):
reasons.queue_no_consumers_nowhen: {queue} has had no consumers since {since} and grows by {perMin} a minute ({ready} ready). {consumer}, connected to RabbitMQ until then, was {how}.
reasons.queue_no_consumers_long: {queue} has had no consumers for more than 6 hours and grows by {perMin} a minute ({ready} ready). {consumer}, which was connected to RabbitMQ, was {how} {when}.
reasons.queue_no_consumers_long_nowhen: {queue} has had no consumers for more than 6 hours and grows by {perMin} a minute ({ready} ready). {consumer}, which was connected to RabbitMQ, was {how}.
reasons.queue_no_consumers_long_unknown: {queue} has had no consumers for more than 6 hours and grows by {perMin} a minute ({ready} ready). No client that was connected to RabbitMQ in the last 24 hours ended in that time.
reasons.autovacuum_not_finishing_plain: Autovacuum isn't finishing on {n} tables: dead rows rose for 24 hours with no autovacuum completed.
reasons.memory_alarm_plain: A node is in a memory alarm: publishers are blocked until memory drops below the high watermark.
reasons.disk_alarm_plain: A node is in a disk alarm: publishers are blocked until free disk is above the limit.
reasons.lock_waits_held: A session waits on a row lock in {table} (for {duration}): {who} holds it, its transaction open for {held}. | {n} sessions wait on row locks in {table} (the longest for {duration}): {who} holds it, its transaction open for {held}.
reasons.connections_refused: {n} connections were refused in the last 15 minutes: max_connections ({max}) was reached.
reasons.replica_stopped: Replication stopped on {member}: its {thread} thread isn't running. {error}
reasons.replica_stopped_plain: Replication stopped: the IO or SQL thread isn't running.
reasons.buffer_pool_hit_low: Only {pct}% of reads come from the InnoDB buffer pool: innodb_buffer_pool_size may be too small for the working set.
reasons.tmp_disk_tables_high: Queries create {perSec} temporary tables on disk a second: sorts and GROUP BY outgrow tmp_table_size.
reasons.performance_schema_off: performance_schema is off (MariaDB's default): statements and their latency stay empty. Set performance_schema=ON in the server's configuration and restart it.
reasons.table_stats_unavailable: WatchLog's user can't read mysql.innodb_table_stats: the largest tables stay empty. GRANT SELECT ON mysql.innodb_table_stats to it.

panels.statementsNote: from performance_schema's digest summary; text only with query text on, as the server normalizes it (values are ?)
